'''Mamikon A. Mnatsakanian''' (17 April 1942 – 12 April 2021<ref>{{cite web |title=Մահացել է հայտնի աստղագետ, պրոֆեսոր Մամիկոն Մնացականյանը |url=https://www.1lurer.am/hy/2021/04/14/%D5%84%D5%A1%D5%B0%D5%A1%D6%81%D5%A5%D5%AC-%D5%A7-%D5%B0%D5%A1%D5%B5%D5%BF%D5%B6%D5%AB-%D5%A1%D5%BD%D5%BF%D5%B2%D5%A1%D5%A3%D5%A5%D5%BF-%D5%BA%D6%80%D5%B8%D6%86%D5%A5%D5%BD%D5%B8%D6%80-%D5%84%D5%A1%D5%B4%D5%AB%D5%AF%D5%B8%D5%B6-%D5%84%D5%B6%D5%A1%D6%81%D5%A1%D5%AF%D5%A1%D5%B6%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6%D5%A8/455258 |website=www.1lurer.am |access-date=5 September 2024 |language=hy |date=14 April 2021}}</ref>) ({{langx|hy|Մամիկոն Մնացականյան}}) was an Armenian physicist.
In 1959, he discovered a new proof of the [[Pythagorean theorem]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://demonstrations.wolfram.com/MamikonsProofOfThePythagoreanTheorem/|title=Mamikon's Proof of the Pythagorean Theorem|publisher=[[Wolfram Demonstrations Project]]}}</ref>

He received a Ph.D. in physics in 1969 from [[Yerevan State University]], where he became professor of astrophysics. As an undergraduate he specialized in the development of geometric methods for solving calculus problems by a visual approach that makes no use of formulas, which he later developed into his system of [[visual calculus]].

He was a Project Associate at [[Project Mathematics!]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]].

With co-author [[Tom M. Apostol|Tom Apostol]], he won the [[Paul R. Halmos – Lester R. Ford Award]] given by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for author excellence, in 2005, 2008, and 2010.

When Apostol met Mamikon he wrote, "As a teacher of calculus for more than 50 years and as an author of a couple of textbooks on the subject, I was stunned to learn that many standard problems in calculus can be easily solved by an innovative visual approach that makes no use of formulas."<ref>{{cite web |title=A Visual Approach to Calculus Problems |url=https://calteches.library.caltech.edu/4007/1/Calculus.pdf |website=Caltech Magazine}}</ref>

In 2010, he was nominated by Caltech for the [[Viktor Hambardzumyan#Ambartsumians International Prize|Ambartsumians International Prize]], awarded annually by the [[President of Armenia]], for his contributions in the field of [[theoretical astrophysics]].<ref>[https://billsexcellentblog.blogspot.com/2010/07/visual-calculus-and-theoretical.html Visual Calculus and Theoretical Astrophysics]</ref>

The book, ''New Horizons in Geometry'', was the result of 15 years of collaboration between Tom Apostol and Mamikon.
